subject: Log-likelihood was decreasing near the ML solution. EM method may be unstable

messages.author: a29b76a7fee2ac43
messages.subject: Log-likelihood was decreasing near the ML solution. EM method may be unstable
parts:
Hi all,

I know this has been discussed in some previous posts and what the message "Log-likelihood was decreasing near the ML solution. EM method may be unstable" possibly means. 

I am trying to decide if this CFA model is worth looking into. The output:

Call:
mirt(data = input_df, model = cfa_model_obj, method = "QMCEM",
    accelerate = "none", technical = list(NCYCLES = 5000, MAXQUAD = 8e+05),
    modeltype = "CFA")

Full-information item factor analysis with 8 factor(s).
Converged within 1e-04 tolerance after 186 QMCEM iterations.
mirt version: 1.39.4
M-step optimizer: BFGS
EM acceleration: none
Number of quasi-Monte Carlo points: 5000
Latent density type: Gaussian

Log-likelihood = -52772.68
Estimated parameters: 470
AIC = 106485.4
BIC = 108490.9; SABIC = 106999
G2 (1e+10) = 98939.73, p = 1
RMSEA = 0, CFI = NaN, TLI = NaN

seems to suggest it converged after 186 iterations. But the warning message took me back a bit.

I assumed the CFI=NaN and TLI=NaN above were output by the default calculation in mIRT which may not necessarily be accurate, that's why I used M2 statistics?

Also, the M2 statistics show it is reasonably ok...



Any suggestion would be much appreciated!

Thanks in advance.

Think of it just as a potential warning flag in case you see the log-likelihood jumping around some modal location. If it decreases slightly that means the M-step is having difficulty updating the current estimates, which could signal a numerical problem, however for the most part this isn't a huge cause for concern if the algorithm appears to have stabilized.
I assumed the CFI=NaN and TLI=NaN above were output by the default calculation in mIRT which may not necessarily be accurate, that's why I used M2 statistics?

Also, the M2 statistics show it is reasonably ok...



Any suggestion would be much appreciated!

Looks fine to me, though the RMSEA and SRMSR are on the high-side of model misfit. HTH.

Phil
